top_evidence.text: A comprehensive literature search yielded a total of 208 articles (Figure 2) relevant to the investigation of interest. Following exclusion based on abstract screening, 16 articles underwent comprehensive full-text review. Ultimately, 13 articles met the prede fi ned inclusion criteria and were included in the analysis, collectively encompassing a cohort of 288 patients. 6,15 -26 12 studies were retrospective, while one study was prospective observational study. Only one study 16 provided data on conventional open surgery as a comparative group, while the other studies exclusively focused on the patients who underwent TEVAR (single group).

top_evidence.document_title: Thoracic endovascular aortic repair for retrograde type a intramural hematoma or aortic dissection with intimal disruption in the descending aorta: Systematic review and meta-analysis
top_evidence.text: The present meta-analysis aimed to investigate outcomes of TEVAR for retrograde extension of the intimal disruption in the descending aorta (RTAAD and RTAIMH) by calculating pooled early and late results from the included studies. To our best knowledge, this is the fi rst meta-analysis that focuses on the use of TEVAR in patients with these critical aortic conditions. Table 1. Study pro fi le of the included studies. AA; ascending aorta, AI; aortic insuf fi ciency, DA; descending aorta, IMH; intramural hematoma, IQR; interquartile range, MC; multicenter, NR; not reported, P; prospective, PAU; penetrating aortic ulcer. R; retrospective, RTAAD; retrograde type A aortic dissection, RTAIMH retrograde type A intramural hematoma, SC; single center, TBAD; type B aortic dissection, ULP; ulcer like projection. Table 2. Perioperative patient characteristics. (continued) Table 2. (continued) CAD; coronary artery disease, CKD; chronic kidney disease, COPD; chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, DM; diabetes mellitus, HTN; hypertension, IQR; interquartile range, NA; not applicable, NR; not reported, TEVAR; thoracic endovascular aortic repair. This study highlights the favorable short-term mortality and perioperative complication rates in patients undergoing TEVAR for RTAAD and RTAIMH with short operation time. Notably, pooled proportion for short-term mortality was only 1%, which is remarkably low compared with open surgery for conventional type A aortic dissection (15 -18%) 27,28 or IMH (7 -10%) 29 -31 reported in the previous studies. Furthermore, the rates of postoperative neurological complications (stroke and spinal cord injury) and aortic-related complications associated with stent-graft placement, such as new intimal tear/aortic dissection progression of the ascending aorta and aortic rupture were remarkably low at 1 -3 %. These favorable short-term outcomes might be attributed to short operation time, less invasive approach without sternotomy, and avoidance of using cardiopulmonary bypass with hypothermic circulatory arrest. However, the time from symptom onset to TEVAR varied across the included studies as seen in Table 1. TEVAR during hyperacute phase (<24 hr) was performed in limited number of patients, who were deemed at high-risk of disease progression or were diagnosed with complicated type B aortic dissection, characterized by presence of hemodynamic instability, aortic rupture, refractory pain or organ malperfusion. The majority of the patients underwent TEVAR during subacute phase (more than 14 days after symptom onset). As they can wait for TEVAR in a stable condition, short-term outcomes might have been favorable in such patients. Regarding late outcomes during the mean follow-up time of about 3.9 years, the aortic reintervention rate and late mortality rate were also satisfactory at 6 and 7%, respectively. The survival rate calculated from reconstructed individual patient data was 93.8% at 3 years and 91.1% at 5 years. Late survival rate was also comparable in the patients of this study compared with patients who underwent open surgery for conventional type A aortic dissection (35 -70%at 5 years) 32 -34 and IMH (87-90% at 5 years). 31,35 Not only favorable survival outcomes, but positive aortic remodeling was observed both in the ascending aorta and descending aorta. Speci fi cally, the diameters of the ascending aorta and descending aorta were signi fi cantly decreased following TEVAR, and the thickness of false lumen or IMH was reduced signi fi cantly as well. As IMH and aortic dissection may have similar but different impacts on the outcomes, subgroup analysis of studies exclusively focusing on RTAIMHwasconducted. The subgroup analysis exhibited the same tendency of the positive aortic remodeling. Considering anatomical similarity of intimal tear location between type B aortic dissection and RTAAD/ RTAIMH, selected patients with RTAAD and RTAIMH could be treated as type B aortic dissection. In other words, patients with complicated features should be treated during hyperacute or acute phase similarly to complicated type B aortic dissection. 3 Although, TEVAR during acute phase is associated with higher short-term complications, including new intimal tear and aortic rupture, possibly due to a more fragile and thinner dissection fl ap, 36 patients in three included studies 18,21,22 underwent TEVAR during the early phase (within 2 days). TEVAR may offer an alternative option to emergent open surgery in this population. On the other hand, patients without complicated features can undergo TEVAR during the subacute phase to mitigate the risk of procedure-related complications similarly to preemptive TEVAR for uncomplicated type B aortic dissection. TEVAR during the subacute phase still offers favorable aortic remodeling because aortic plasticity may be maintained up to 3 months from onset (subacute phase). 37,38

top_evidence.section: Risk Of Bias In Individual Studies
top_evidence.text: The Cochrane tool Risk of Bias Assessment Tool for Nonrandomized Studies 14 was employed to evaluate the quality of the studies in this meta-analysis. Two independent authors (N.N. and H.T.) conducted the assessment, resolving any discrepancies or con fl icts through consensus. The outcomes of the assessment were visually presented using the ' Robvis ' package in the R software. Evaluation of publication bias was conducted using funnel plots, which provide a visual representation of the distribution of study outcomes. Asymmetry in the funnel plots was assessed using the linear regression test, 12 employing modi fi ed standard error as suggested by Pustejovsky et al. 13 A signi fi cance level of p < .1 indicated the presence of publication bias.

top_evidence.document_title: Thoracic endovascular aortic repair for retrograde type a intramural hematoma or aortic dissection with intimal disruption in the descending aorta: Systematic review and meta-analysis
top_evidence.text: The selection of articles adhered to stringent inclusion criteria, encompassing original studies reporting the short-term or long-term outcomes of the use of TEVAR for RTAAD or RTAIMH. Exclusion criteria included review articles, case reports, and investigations involving animal subjects. Additionally, studies not documented in the English language were excluded from consideration.
